label: History
value: Anne grew up as an orphan.
unit: Anne grew up as an orphan after her parents passed away from fever in Bolingbroke during her infancy. She attended Queen's Academy, where she took the Second Year course to earn a First Class teacher's license in one year and competed vigorously against Gilbert Blythe for academic honors like the Avery scholarship. During her time in school, she built close friendships with classmates such as Stella Maynard and Priscilla Grant, while maintaining a strong bond with her childhood friend Diana Barry. After completing her studies, Anne taught school for three years in Summerside. During a fortnight's stay in Bolingbroke, she visited her birth house, met the current tenant, and was given a packet of her mother's old letters. She later moved to Four Winds after becoming engaged to Gilbert Blythe, where she resided in a small white house she named her 'house of dreams' and befriended neighbors such as Leslie Moore and Captain Jim. Following three years of teaching in Summerside, she prepared to marry Gilbert.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School.
unit: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School, where he sits by himself at a corner desk in the classroom. When Anne Shirley becomes his teacher, he stares at her with hostile black eyes, having previously only had male teachers and believing that female teachers are no good. During one of his early days under Anne's instruction, he pours the last drops of water from his slate bottle down Aurelia Clay's neck, after which Anne keeps him in at recess to give him a lecture on how gentlemen ought to behave. Though Anne attempts to win his affection through patience and kindness, Anthony continues to obey her with a scornful air of toleration. However, after Anne eventually administers a whipping to him, Anthony decides she is worth something after all, remarking that the whipping was as good as a man's.

label: Personality
value: Aunt Jamesina possesses a cheerful disposition.
unit: Aunt Jamesina possesses a cheerful, indulgent, and youthful disposition. She is open about being old-fashioned in her style and opinions, preferring comfort over formality. Charming and patient, she acts as a forgiving housemother who lets the young women make their own choices while maintaining her own dry humor. She candidly owns up to her own past flaws and likes to joke about her former and current suitors.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina's only daughter married.
unit: After her only daughter married and left for missionary work, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. At the suggestion of her niece Stella Maynard, she agreed to move to Kingsport to act as housemother for Stella, Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. She brought along her cat, the Sarah-cat, as well as Joseph, a colorful cat entrusted to her by a friend moving to Vancouver. Upon moving into Patty's Place, she quickly won the deep affection of the four students. During her time in Kingsport, she presided over the household with gentle humor, listened to the young women's romantic dilemmas, shared anecdotes of her own past suitors, and kept up correspondence with old widowers back home who held affection for her.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea alongside his sister Jane and other local youth. After his father deeded him the upper farm, he sought to get married. Due to his extreme shyness, he enlisted his sister Jane to propose to Anne Shirley on his behalf during a winter visit, offering to wait until she finished college if necessary. Following Anne's refusal, he turned his affections to Nettie Blewett, whom he eventually married. The couple later made a proud public appearance together at church in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Captain Jim spent the majority of his life at sea.
unit: Captain Jim spent the majority of his life at sea, traveling to remote corners of the world and surviving wild adventures including mutinies, shipwrecks, Malay pirates, and shipwreck on the Magdalens. Five years before retiring to the Four Winds Point lighthouse, he ceased his ocean voyages and settled into the life of a lightkeeper, living simply with his cat, Matey, whom he had rescued from freezing. He formed close bonds with local residents, including Elizabeth Russell, Miss Cornelia Bryant, and later Anne and Gilbert Blythe. When Owen Ford visited Four Winds, Captain Jim shared his treasured 'life-book' manuscript with him. Owen Ford adapted the manuscript into a published book titled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim', listing Captain Jim as a collaborator. On the evening after receiving his published book, Captain Jim celebrated with Anne and Leslie Moore before passing away peacefully in his home.

Owen Ford adapted the manuscript into a published book titled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim', listing Captain Jim as a collaborator. On the evening after receiving his published book, Captain Jim celebrated with Anne and Leslie Moore before passing away peacefully in his home.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth is named Leonora Bowman.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth, whose real name is Leonora Bowman, came to live at Echo Lodge as a domestic handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis, following in the footsteps of her three elder sisters. Unlike her sisters, she tolerates and never mocks Miss Lavendar's imaginative pretendings. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visit Echo Lodge, Charlotta assists in demonstrating the famous woodland echoes by blowing a tin horn and laughing. She worries deeply about Miss Lavendar's health and emotional state, confiding her fears to Anne when Miss Lavendar accidentally cracks a prized pink teacup. When Stephen Irving arrives to reunite with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta demands that Anne explain the situation in plain prose, openly wishing for their marriage so Miss Lavendar will not be left alone when Charlotta eventually leaves for Boston. In the days leading up to Miss Lavendar's wedding, Charlotta works frantically to decorate, polish silver, and prepare food while worrying about potential disasters like rain or sudden illnesses. On the wedding day, she dresses in her finest starched gown and crinkly plaited hair, satisfied with her work and relieved that the occasion proceeds smoothly.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Miss Cornelia Bryant grew up in Four Winds, where she had many suitors in her youth but maintained a sharp disdain for men. Over the years, she established herself as an indispensable community figure, always stepping in to assist neighbors in distress and sew clothing for families in need. After Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved into their house of dreams at Four Winds, Miss Cornelia promptly called on them, bringing hand-embroidered baby clothes she was sewing for a local family. She quickly became a close friend and frequent visitor to Anne, sharing local news, entertaining anecdotes, and the tragic past of her best friend, Leslie Moore. Eventually, Miss Cornelia surprised her community by marrying Marshall Elliott.

Over the years, she established herself as an indispensable community figure, always stepping in to assist neighbors in distress and sew clothing for families in need. After Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved into their house of dreams at Four Winds, Miss Cornelia promptly called on them, bringing hand-embroidered baby clothes she was sewing for a local family. She quickly became a close friend and frequent visitor to Anne, sharing local news, entertaining anecdotes, and the tragic past of her best friend, Leslie Moore. Eventually, Miss Cornelia surprised her community by marrying Marshall Elliott.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned and eventually brought to Green Gables to live with Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley. Upon his arrival, Davy immediately showed a lively, unruly disposition, often testing Marilla's patience with his candid remarks and table manners. Unlike his quiet sister, Davy bonded warmly with Anne, who guided his behavior with gentleness and imagination. Following the death of his uncle, Richard Keith, a trust fund was established to cover Davy and Dora's living expenses, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. Davy attended Avonlea School, where he engaged in outdoor adventures with classmates like Milty Boulter and developed an innocent childhood crush on Stella Fletcher.

As she grew older, Diana remained Anne's constant companion in Avonlea, though she did not pursue higher education after school. She married Fred Wright and settled down in Avonlea, eventually giving birth to her firstborn son, little Fred.

label: History
value: Dick Moore worked at his father Abner's store in the winters.
unit: Dick Moore worked at his father Abner's store at the Glen in the winters and sailed during the summers. He became infatuated with Leslie West due to her beauty, but she repeatedly spurned his advances. To force her into marriage, Dick threatened to have his father foreclose the overdue mortgage on the West farm, prompting Leslie's mother to pressure Leslie into marrying him. Following their quiet wedding, Dick and Leslie lived on the West farm for the winter. In the spring, after Leslie's mother passed away, Dick grew tired of quiet married life and left for Nova Scotia. There, he joined his cousin, George Moore, on a trading voyage aboard the Four Sisters bound for Havana, Cuba. Upon reaching Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to sail without him, while George stayed behind to nurse him. For thirteen years, the people of Four Winds mistakenly believed that George Moore—who was brought back suffering from severe amnesia and brain damage—was Dick Moore.

unit: Dick Moore worked at his father Abner's store at the Glen in the winters and sailed during the summers. He became infatuated with Leslie West due to her beauty, but she repeatedly spurned his advances. To force her into marriage, Dick threatened to have his father foreclose the overdue mortgage on the West farm, prompting Leslie's mother to pressure Leslie into marrying him. Following their quiet wedding, Dick and Leslie lived on the West farm for the winter. In the spring, after Leslie's mother passed away, Dick grew tired of quiet married life and left for Nova Scotia. There, he joined his cousin, George Moore, on a trading voyage aboard the Four Sisters bound for Havana, Cuba. Upon reaching Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to sail without him, while George stayed behind to nurse him. For thirteen years, the people of Four Winds mistakenly believed that George Moore—who was brought back suffering from severe amnesia and brain damage—was Dick Moore.

value: Following the illness of Mary Keith, Dora was taken in by Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Following the illness and death of her mother Mary Keith, Dora and her twin brother Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert to live at Green Gables. She quickly proved to be a quiet, polite, and prim child, in contrast to her mischievous twin brother. Upon starting school, she sat with Mirabel Cotton, who frightened her with stories of deceased relatives walking about houses. On another occasion, her brother Davy locked her in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse and lied about her whereabouts until Anne Shirley rescued her. As she grew up at Green Gables, Dora maintained her polite, moral demeanour and refused to associate with unruly children like the Cottons.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta due to his father's illness. On his return to school, he tried to get Anne Shirley's attention by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots', sparking an intense academic rivalry that lasted for years. Despite Anne snubbing his early attempts to reconcile, Gilbert continued to harbor deep affection for her while excelling at Avonlea School. He went on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport, where he served as Freshman Class president, led his class to victory in the annual Arts Rush, and joined the 'Lambs' fraternity. During his college years, he suffered a severe bout of typhoid fever at home in Avonlea, which ultimately brought about Anne's realization of her love for him. After finishing his education and becoming a doctor, Gilbert married Anne, and the couple established their home at Four Winds Point.

value: Mr. Harrison is crusty.
unit: A crusty, crabbed, and outspoken man who admits to being lonesome, Mr. Harrison possesses a sharp temper and an unusual habit of blunt honesty that often offends his neighbors. He takes a pragmatic view of life, prefers keeping to himself without women around his home, and can be quite nervous when caught off guard or when admitting fault. Despite his crusty exterior, he enjoys the youthful energy of Anne Shirley, shows a kind heart toward his pet, and can prove quite mild, friendly, and neighborly once acquainted with others.

label: History
value: Before Anne Shirley returned home from Queen's, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables in Avonlea
unit: Before Anne Shirley returned home from Queen's, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables in Avonlea and moved in as a newcomer from New Brunswick. He quickly gained a local reputation as an odd 'crank' for keeping house by himself, lacking set mealtimes, only washing dishes in rain barrels on wet Sundays, and making outspoken remarks to local figures like Mrs. Rachel Lynde. One day, after angrily confronting Anne when her Jersey cow strayed onto his grain, he received a visit from her to confess that she had accidentally sold his cow by mistake. Though initial tension arose when his parrot insulted her, he treated Anne politely, invited her inside, and enjoyed tea with her after she cleared up the misunderstanding and washed his dishes. Over time, Mr. Harrison formed a warm friendship with Anne, engaging in discussions about the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and local affairs on his veranda. During these visits, he frequently voiced his candid opinions on truthfulness and community figures while admitting that spending time with Anne made him feel young again.

He quickly gained a local reputation as an odd 'crank' for keeping house by himself, lacking set mealtimes, only washing dishes in rain barrels on wet Sundays, and making outspoken remarks to local figures like Mrs. Rachel Lynde. One day, after angrily confronting Anne when her Jersey cow strayed onto his grain, he received a visit from her to confess that she had accidentally sold his cow by mistake. Though initial tension arose when his parrot insulted her, he treated Anne politely, invited her inside, and enjoyed tea with her after she cleared up the misunderstanding and washed his dishes. Over time, Mr. Harrison formed a warm friendship with Anne, engaging in discussions about the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and local affairs on his veranda. During these visits, he frequently voiced his candid opinions on truthfulness and community figures while admitting that spending time with Anne made him feel young again.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea and attended school alongside Anne Shirley and her circle of friends. She participated in local childhood games, including a dramatization of Tennyson's Elaine on the pond. Later, she attended Queen's Academy in Kingsport to study for her teacher's license, though she often found teaching to be monotonous. After her education, she engaged in teaching work. Eventually, she met and married Mr. Inglis, a wealthy English millionaire who had made money in mines. Despite her newfound wealth and silken, jewel-adorned lifestyle, she returned to Avonlea prior to Anne's wedding to visit her old friends, remaining as amiable, un-spoiled, and interested in Anne's happiness as ever.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar lived in seclusion

Living out of the public eye, she entertained herself with imaginary companions, including a 'little dream-boy,' assisted by her young handmaiden, Charlotta the Fourth. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, Miss Lavendar welcomed them warmly and formed an immediate, lasting bond with Anne. After discovering that Anne was the schoolteacher of Paul Irving—the son of her former fiancé Stephen Irving—she eventually agreed to meet the boy. She quickly grew fond of Paul, entertaining him at her home and treating him as a particular friend.

label: History
value: Leslie cared for a brain-damaged man
unit: Leslie spent years caring for a brain-damaged man brought home by Captain Jim, whom everyone believed to be her husband Dick Moore. After becoming close neighbors with Anne Shirley at Four Winds, Leslie developed a deep friendship with her and found solace visiting the little house of dreams. Upon learning from Gilbert Blythe and Captain Jim that a medical operation might restore the man's lost faculties, Leslie mortgaged her farm to Captain Jim to fund a trip to a Montreal hospital. The operation proved successful and restored his memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's double cousin, George Moore, and that the real Dick Moore had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Free from her tragic burden, Leslie returned home to adjust to her new life and stayed with Anne at the little house of dreams while courted by Owen Ford.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott vowed not to cut his hair.
unit: During a particularly bitter general election fifteen years earlier, Marshall Elliott publicly vowed never to cut his hair or shave his face until the Liberal (Grit) party came to power. Because the Liberals remained out of office, he faithfully kept his vow for fifteen years, giving him an unusually shaggy, freakish appearance. During this time, he spent time with Captain Jim, going cod-fishing, singing old ballads, and dancing rhythmically at social gatherings around Four Winds. When the election results finally brought the Liberals to power, Marshall quietly walked to Augustus Palmer's barber shop late at night, forced the sleeping barber to open the shop, and had his hair and beard trimmed under the condition that political matters were not discussed. Shortly after changing his appearance, he met Anne Shirley at the lighthouse, silently enjoying the joke that she failed to recognize him. Later that summer, Marshall became engaged to Miss Cornelia Bryant and agreed to live at her property after their wedding.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables in Avonlea alongside his sister Marilla. Intending to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work, Matthew drove to Bright River station, where he instead encountered Anne Shirley. Unable to turn her away, he brought her back to Green Gables and convinced Marilla that they should raise and educate her. Over the following years, Matthew served as Anne's quiet advocate and supporter, encouraging her studies for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy. For Christmas one year, despite his terror of shopping and dealing with clerks, he arranged through Mrs. Rachel Lynde to buy Anne a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves. Years later, after returning home from the post office, Matthew collapsed and died instantly at the doorway from the shock of reading a newspaper report detailing the failure of the Abbey Bank.

label: History
value: Owen Ford arrives in Four Winds
unit: Owen Ford arrives in Four Winds to spend his summer holiday, driven by a desire to visit his mother's childhood home. He sets up a workshop in a small room at the lighthouse, writing every morning with feverish enthusiasm and spending his afternoons enjoying outings with Anne Blythe, Gilbert, Captain Jim, and Leslie. As the summer progresses, Owen falls deeply in love with Leslie, endowing the female protagonist of his novel with her personality. Near the end of his stay, after finishing his manuscript, he confesses his intense love for Leslie to Anne, expressing heartbreak over Leslie's unhappy marriage while resolving to act honorably and leave in silence. Shortly before his departure, he meets Leslie alone in the garden of the little house, where the two express their mutual love, share a kiss, and crown her hair with a red rose. He later receives Captain Jim's affectionate blessing alongside Leslie, Anne, and Gilbert before leaving Four Winds.

label: History
value: Following the death of his mother, Paul was sent from Boston to Avonlea.
unit: Following the death of his mother, Paul was sent from Boston to Avonlea to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving. He enrolled in the local school under the instruction of Anne Shirley, with whom he formed a swift and affectionate bond based on their mutual love for imaginative fancies. During his time at school, he engaged in a drawn battle with St. Clair Donnell to defend his American patriotism and stood up as a gentlemanly and protective figure among his peers. He also made regular visits to Miss Lavendar at Echo Lodge, connecting with her over her concept of a 'dream-boy' and sharing his tales of rock people and dream worlds. After two years in Avonlea, his father Stephen Irving returned, rekindling his romance with Miss Lavendar. Following their marriage, Paul moved to Boston alongside Charlotta the Fourth to reside with his father and stepmother, with plans to later study abroad for two years.

He also made regular visits to Miss Lavendar at Echo Lodge, connecting with her over her concept of a 'dream-boy' and sharing his tales of rock people and dream worlds. After two years in Avonlea, his father Stephen Irving returned, rekindling his romance with Miss Lavendar. Following their marriage, Paul moved to Boston alongside Charlotta the Fourth to reside with his father and stepmother, with plans to later study abroad for two years.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Philippa Gordon was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to a prominent and wealthy family. Upon arriving at Redmond College, she quickly became a central figure in social life due to her background, beauty, and charming personality. She first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in an old graveyard near campus, instantly deciding to become close friends with them. Throughout her first year at Redmond, she introduced Anne and Priscilla to her wide circle of friends and social gatherings. She regularly shared tales of her numerous suitors, particularly her two primary hometown admirers, Alec and Alonzo, whom she struggled to choose between. Over time, she moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, and Aunt Jamesina. Eventually, Philippa abandoned her superficial romantic criteria and chose to marry Jonas 'Jo' Blake.

Upon arriving at Redmond College, she quickly became a central figure in social life due to her background, beauty, and charming personality. She first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in an old graveyard near campus, instantly deciding to become close friends with them. Throughout her first year at Redmond, she introduced Anne and Priscilla to her wide circle of friends and social gatherings. She regularly shared tales of her numerous suitors, particularly her two primary hometown admirers, Alec and Alonzo, whom she struggled to choose between. Over time, she moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, and Aunt Jamesina. Eventually, Philippa abandoned her superficial romantic criteria and chose to marry Jonas 'Jo' Blake.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school. During his time teaching, he paid special attention to Prissy Andrews, often helping her with Latin and algebra problems while the rest of the scholars behaved as they pleased. He punished Gilbert Blythe and Ruby Gillis for classroom disruptions, and he famously called Anne Shirley 'Carrots' and punished her by making her sit with the boys, causing Anne to refuse to return to his school for a time. Although not considered an exceptionally good teacher by some, his pupils still made academic progress under his instruction. Upon his eventual departure from the Avonlea school, some students weeping was noted.

label: History
value: Priscilla taught school in Carmody.
unit: Priscilla formerly taught school in Carmody before deciding to pursue higher education. She visited Anne Shirley at Green Gables accompanied by her aunt, Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, and Mrs. Pendexter. Later, she traveled to Kingsport to begin her studies at Redmond College, meeting Anne upon her arrival at the train station and guiding her to their shared boardinghouse on St. John Street. She quickly became part of a close-knit group of friends alongside Anne and Philippa Gordon, integrating into Redmond's social scene. Seeking a better living arrangement than a boardinghouse, Priscilla and Anne went house-hunting around Kingsport and ultimately succeeded in renting Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue to live with their friends.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Avonlea
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Avonlea as a long-time neighbor and close friend of Marilla Cuthbert. When Marilla took in the young orphan Anne Shirley, Rachel criticized Anne's freckles and red hair, provoking an explosive outburst of temper from the young girl; however, she later forgave Anne after receiving a dramatic apology. Throughout Anne's youth, Rachel remained a central pillar of community news and church fundraising. After her husband Thomas passed away quietly following a long illness, Rachel faced severe financial strain due to farm mortgages and medical costs, threatening to force her to leave Avonlea. To keep her friend in the community and allow Anne to attend college, Marilla invited Rachel to move into Green Gables. Rachel gratefully accepted, establishing a home in the north gable and taking over domestic care for Marilla and the Keith twins.

Throughout Anne's youth, Rachel remained a central pillar of community news and church fundraising. After her husband Thomas passed away quietly following a long illness, Rachel faced severe financial strain due to farm mortgages and medical costs, threatening to force her to leave Avonlea. To keep her friend in the community and allow Anne to attend college, Marilla invited Rachel to move into Green Gables. Rachel gratefully accepted, establishing a home in the north gable and taking over domestic care for Marilla and the Keith twins.

label: History
value: Royal Gardner paused his college studies.
unit: Royal Gardner was forced to pause his college studies for two years to travel abroad with his ailing mother. After returning to his studies, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a rainstorm when her umbrella turned inside out, rescuing her with his own. He immediately began courting her by sending long-stemmed roses, accompanied by poetic lines. Over two years, Roy pursued Anne with romantic gestures, sending orchids to her receptions and visiting her regularly at Patty's Place. He eventually took Anne to the seaside pavilion on the harbor shore where they had first talked and proposed to her with carefully chosen words. When Anne unexpectedly rejected his proposal because she did not love him, Roy was stunned and deeply hurt, stating that she had ruined his life before bidding her a final farewell.

After returning to his studies, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a rainstorm when her umbrella turned inside out, rescuing her with his own. He immediately began courting her by sending long-stemmed roses, accompanied by poetic lines. Over two years, Roy pursued Anne with romantic gestures, sending orchids to her receptions and visiting her regularly at Patty's Place. He eventually took Anne to the seaside pavilion on the harbor shore where they had first talked and proposed to her with carefully chosen words. When Anne unexpectedly rejected his proposal because she did not love him, Roy was stunned and deeply hurt, stating that she had ruined his life before bidding her a final farewell.

value: Ruby is cheerful.

Though prone to laughing and chattering, she can be easily frightened or nervous, as shown by her dread of play-acting or death. When faced with a fatal illness, she fought desperately to maintain a hopeful, gay mask to hide her terror.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea as a schoolmate and playfellow of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. During a summer outing by Orchard Slope pond, she joined her friends in dramatizing Tennyson's Elaine, though she declined to play the title role due to fear of lying down pretending to be dead. Later, she attended Queen's Academy alongside her Avonlea peers and was widely recognized as the handsomest girl in her year. During this period, Gilbert Blythe frequently accompanied her home on weekends and carried her satchel, though she found his intellectual conversations confusing compared to other suitors. After completing her studies, she took up teaching as a profession. However, she contracted galloping consumption during the winter, forcing her to step down from teaching while harboring hopes of securing the White Sands school in the fall. Throughout the following summer, she clung to a mask of giddiness and constantly talked about her suitors, while secretly struggling with the terrifying knowledge of her approaching end. One evening in the garden, she confessed her deep fear of dying and leaving her accustomed life to Anne. Shortly after, she passed away quietly in her sleep and was buried in a white velvet casket in the Avonlea graveyard.

label: History
value: Miss Stacy serves as the schoolteacher at Avonlea
unit: Miss Stacy serves as the schoolteacher at Avonlea, succeeding Mr. Phillips. During her tenure, she takes a keen interest in her students' moral and intellectual development, guiding teenage girls on character formation and monitoring their reading choices. When catching Anne Shirley reading a novel during class, she gently explains the wrongdoing of deceit and time-wasting rather than administering harsh punishment. Recognizing the potential of her advanced pupils, she organizes a specialized Queen's Academy entrance class, offering extra daily instruction after regular school hours and visiting parents like Marilla Cuthbert to secure permission. Though offered a teaching post in her home district, she chooses to return to Avonlea due to her strong attachment to her students. She guides her Queen's class through their studies, offering practical advice and support up to their entrance examinations before her tenure in Avonlea ultimately ends.

value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, completing her third year before taking up a teaching position at a back country school. After teaching for two years, she grew tired of the demands and financial trials of being a country schoolteacher and decided to quit to pursue higher education at Redmond College. Preferring independent living over boardinghouses, she wrote to Anne proposed that she, Anne, and Priscilla rent a furnished house in Kingsport together. To manage the household, Stella arranged for her widowed aunt, Aunt Jamesina, to join them as their housekeeper.

label: History
value: Susan Baker is an elderly spinster
unit: Susan Baker, an elderly spinster living in the Glen, was installed as a maid-of-all-work at the little house of dreams for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and his wife Anne. Within a few weeks of her arrival, she came to adore young Mrs. Doctor with blind fervor. When Marilla Cuthbert arrived prior to the birth of Anne's first child, Susan initially regarded her with slight jealousy before reconciling with her after realizing Marilla would not interfere in kitchen affairs. During the tense night of Anne's labor, Susan sat in the kitchen with cotton wool in her ears and an apron over her head while praying fiercely for Anne's safety. Following the child's birth, Susan immediately took charge of domestic affairs so Anne could focus on her baby. When the infant tragically died, Susan wept alongside Marilla out of heartbreak for Anne. She continued her steadfast service to the Blythe family, engaging in conversations about local marriages and community affairs with Anne and Miss Cornelia Bryant.

Within a few weeks of her arrival, she came to adore young Mrs. Doctor with blind fervor. When the infant tragically died, Susan wept alongside Marilla out of heartbreak for Anne. She continued her steadfast service to the Blythe family, engaging in conversations about local marriages and community affairs with Anne and Miss Cornelia Bryant.
